findings.reason: a node implementing the rule literally repoints only patches of moved names, leaves the routing.os/routing.shutil patch targets in place, and the gate then goes red on those files with the plan giving no instruction for them; the rule must be rekeyed on the module the moved function reads a name from, not on whether the name moved.
findings.text: the deliverable says "Some tests read routing.py's source text or patch a moved name on routing. Each such test is repointed to the module that now defines the name", but the process-signalling and gc code that moves is intercepted by tests patching names that do NOT move: tests/test_every_signal_leaves_a_sender_record.py:76,78,118,119,173,174 patch routing.os.kill/killpg, tests/test_unwatch_leaves_a_sender_record.py:136 patches routing.os.killpg, tests/test_worker_signal_reach.py:20-22,59 patch routing.os.getpgid/killpg/kill, and tests/test_gc_sweeps_orphan_scratch.py:89 patches routing.shutil.rmtree (with wraps=routing.shutil.rmtree). After gc.py/process_signal.py are created with their own `import os`/`import shutil`, the moved bodies read their own module's bindings, so patching routing.os/routing.shutil no longer intercepts them — the calls proceed to real os.kill/killpg/shutil.rmtree, which is exactly what those tests arm the patch to prevent (test_every_signal_leaves_a_sender_record.py's own docstring: "The signal is not delivered — both os.kill and os.killpg are recorded instead — so the child survives to be inspected")

findings.reason: the conclusion the figures support still holds with margin (routing.py's remainder measures 42,653 tokens, under the 50,000 bound and near the stated ~44,000), so no node's path changes; the figures are understated but not decision-bearing.
findings.text: the two family token figures do not reproduce under the repository's own instrument: summing the source of the twelve named gc statements gives 40,402 bytes (39.5 KB, ~11,544 tokens) against the stated "about 38.7 KB", and the thirteen named process-signalling statements give 19,122 bytes (18.7 KB, ~5,464 tokens) against the stated "about 16.6 KB"; combined 59,524 bytes = ~17,007 tokens against the stated "about 15,800", and the plan's figures are floors because the gc list additionally carries "the constants only they use", which the plan does not count
